title: Lust
desc_lfm_album: Lust is the debut album by Belgian electronic band Lords of Acid, released in 1991. The band had released several 12-inch singles prior to their full-legth debut, and these songs ("I Sit on Acid" and "Hey Ho!") were already dance club hits. Continuing with their outrageous sexually-explicit, always tongue-in-cheek, often humorous lyrical themes, Lust presented an album's worth of techno and rave anthems that earned positive reviews from music critics, both in and out of the dance music community. desc_lfm_artist: Lords of Acid is a Belgian-American post-industrial/techno band, led by musician Praga Khan. They debuted with the controversial new beat single "I Sit on Acid" in 1988. Created by Jade 4U, Praga Khan and Olivier Adams; their debut album, 1991's Lust (along with additional singles "Rough Sex" and "I Must Increase My Bust"), were critically acclaimed within the electronic music and dance music communities for their outrageously sexual lyrics and sound samples.

title: Intermix
desc_lfm_artist:
Intermix was an electronic music group in the 1990s, and consisted of Bill Leeb and Rhys Fulber.

Unlike their other projects (including Front Line Assembly, Noise Unit, and Delerium), Intermix shows somewhat more of a techno influence, while Delerium is more mellow and ambient, and Front Line Assembly has a very industrial style.

The first two albums Intermix released sound very much like their related project Delerium, albeit with a much more prevalent techno influence.
